crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Drafting proposal responses covers the work of turning a request for proposal, a request for information, or a similar bid document into a structured first draft that a human team can edit and submit. In finance it appears in vendor onboarding, custody and fund administration pitches, data licensing, and technology procurement, where the response must answer dozens of numbered requirements in the buyer's own format. The scope runs from reading the questions and mapping them to existing material, through assembling answers, to flagging the gaps that only a subject matter expert can close.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on a retrieval layer over the firm's past responses, product documentation, security questionnaires, and approved boilerplate, plus a drafting model that writes into a template. Teams typically keep the source library in a document store or wiki, use a structured export such as a spreadsheet or a form for the question set, and track versions so that reviewers can see what changed between drafts. Access controls matter because the library often contains pricing, client names, and unpublished roadmap detail.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: A common pattern is to parse the bid document into individual requirements, classify each one, retrieve the closest approved passages, and generate a draft answer with a citation back to the source. Reviewers then accept, edit, or reject each answer, and the rejected ones become the gap list for experts. The output is a working draft, not a submission, and the useful measure is how much editing a reviewer has to do rather than how fluent the text reads.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Provenance is the central control: every generated answer should point to the source passage it came from, and any claim about certifications, service levels, or past performance should be traceable to an approved record. Firms also need rules on what the system may never assert on its own, such as pricing, legal commitments, or security guarantees, and a named human owner for the final document. Because responses often contain confidential client and commercial information, retention and access rules apply to the drafts and to the retrieval index alike.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction of travel is toward tighter integration with the systems that hold the underlying facts, so that answers about controls, uptime, and references are pulled from live records rather than from old documents. Expect more emphasis on audit trails that show which passages a draft drew on and who approved each answer, and on evaluation sets built from past bids to check whether retrieval is finding the right material. The human role is likely to shift further toward reviewing exceptions and owning the commercial judgment calls.
